evals.prompt: Run a doc-comment pass on the Go package in evals/files/docs/. Go style (comment starts with the identifier name), public = capitalized identifier, verify with `go build ./...`, revert with git checkout, cap 12 iterations.
evals.expected_output: Discovery list of exported declarations missing/deficient docs, prioritized; proportional fixes applied via Edit; build verified; report with counts.
expectations: Every exported identifier in store.go without a doc comment is listed in the discovery phase
Fixes are applied with Edit after reading the file; the file is not rewritten wholesale
Added Go doc comments start with the identifier name
The unexported helper `clamp` is not given a doc comment (out of scope)
The final report states the number discovered, fixed, and skipped, and the verify command result

evals.prompt: docs pass on evals/files/docs/ but the codebase has hundreds of files and i only have 5 iterations. what do you fix first?
evals.expected_output: Prioritization by impact (package-level docs and most-referenced exported types first), an explicit statement of what is deferred, and only proportional fixes within the budget.
expectations: The response explains the prioritization order it applied
Work stops within the stated iteration budget and the report names what was not reached
No speculative or padded doc comments are added to already-adequate declarations
